lines.ruling: Ruling: scope; as the prior rulings. i1040sca p. 2, Line 1: "Any person you could have claimed as a dependent except that you or your spouse if filing jointly can be claimed as a dependent on someone else's 2025 return." The case cannot reach line 1: a filer who, or whose joint spouse, can be claimed as a dependent is refused by sa.dependent on sa.standard and sa.deduction, the deduction Form 1040 line 12e reads, so no completed return has that person's expenses. The reply agrees the zero for a filer whose costs were not over 7.5% leaves line 4 unchanged. Project stands.

Ruling: scope; refusal located elsewhere. i1040sca p. 8, Line 8a, 'subtract the amount shown on Form 8396, line 3, from the total deductible interest'. A mortgage credit certificate is asked by s3.mcc when mortgage interest is entered and refuses Schedule 3 line 7 and the return through s3.mcc_if_interest (Form 8396), so no computed return reaches line 8a with the credit (fixture redesign.credits.refuse.mcc). The shared-interest point of the earlier round is now in the input's label ('only your share of a loan shared with someone other than your spouse'). Project stands on the English.

Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.sa_medical_negative_agi: the project floors adjusted gross income at zero for the 7.5% medical limit (a negative line 2 would raise line 4 above the expenses), the recorded reading; same ruling as the earlier rounds. f1040sa line 2, "Enter amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b".

Ruling: finding; low; the model is right that deductible foreign taxes that are not creditable are neither computed nor refused. p514 p. 3, Exceptions for foreign taxes not allowed as a credit: "Even if you claim a credit for other foreign taxes, you can deduct any foreign tax that is not allowed as a credit if you did any of the following", including "You paid withholding tax on dividends from foreign corporations whose stock you did not hold for the required period of time". ftc.taxes asks only creditable taxes and sa.foreign_tax_deduct is asked only when they are positive (ftc.has_tax), so line 6 is $0 for such a filer with no refusal. The GST part of the model's reason stays refused: GST on income distributions reaches the filer through a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), and scope.k1 (estates and trusts included) still refuses through scope.schedule1 (checked on the current forms). (BUG-0768)

Ruling: scope; i1040sca p. 11, Line 15, "Complete and attach Form 4684 to figure the amount of your loss". A casualty or theft is refused before Schedule A: sd.casualty (asked of every filer) feeds sd.other_forms, refused on Schedule D and from Form 1040 line 7a on, so line 15 is $0 on every computed return; the line's citation names that refusal (fix of BUG-0639). Same ruling as the earlier round (2026-11-14); checked on the current forms.

Ruling: scope; i1040sca p. 11, Line 16 list. The gambling limit matches, as the model says. Casualty and theft losses of income-producing property (Form 4684 lines 32 and 38b, Form 4797 line 18a) and a net qualified disaster loss (Form 4684 line 15) are refused through sd.casualty and sd.business_property into sd.other_forms; the claim-of-right repayment over $3,000 by s3.repaid_income (Schedule 3 and scope refusals); the other listed items by sa.unsupported. Same ruling as the earlier round (2026-11-14); gates checked on the current forms.

Ruling: representation; the model asks whether a filer may deduct investment interest without Form 4952 and get zero. f4952 (2025) p. 3, Who Must File: "you must file Form 4952 to claim a deduction for your investment interest expense. Exception. You don’t have to file Form 4952 if all of the following apply" (investment income from interest and ordinary dividends less qualified dividends above the expense, no other deductible investment expenses, no 2024 carryover). Such a filer still has investment interest on Form 4952 line 1 above zero, so f4952.used is true and f4952.line8 is the smaller of lines 3 and 6, which under the exception's first condition is the whole interest: the form is used as the computation, whether or not it is filed (f4952.required). Line 8 is zero only with no investment interest, no carryforward and no election, when there is nothing to deduct. Inspected in forms/2025/f4952.yaml (f4952.used, f4952.line8) after PENDING-6 of the credits-misc package.

Ruling: finding; medium; the model is right in part: the worksheet's earned income is "Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 1z, and Schedule 1, lines 3, 6, 8r, 8t, and 8u minus the amount, if any, on Schedule 1, line 15" (i1040gi p. 35, Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents) and sa.dep_earned_sum leaves out 6, 8t and 8u. Lines 6 (Schedule F, scope.farm in scope.schedule1) and 8t (s1.nqdc_pension_if_w2 in s1.line8_other) are still refused, so they are zero on every computed return (amb.2025.sa_dep_earned). Line 8u is not: lane x2-s1o made it computed, so a dependent filer with wages earned while an inmate has line 2 too small. (BUG-0767)

Ruling: scope; the model says the count of boxes omits a spouse's boxes on a married filing separately return when the spouse had no income, files no return and can't be claimed (i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d). That case is refused: sa.mfs_spouse_extra ("Married filing separately and claiming age or blindness boxes for your spouse", asked when the spouse is not itemizing) refuses on sa.standard, which reads this worksheet ("Standard Deduction Chart spouse boxes on a separate return"). On every computed return the boxes are the filer's and, on a joint return, the spouse's.
